content.title: About
content.content: A milk shake is a cold beverage made from milk, cream and various flavorings, commonly served in fast‑food restaurants. Non‑chocolate versions include vanilla, strawberry, banana, caramel and nut flavors.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first milk shake appeared in the United States in the early 20th century as a "milk frappe".
In Russia the milk shake became popular in the 1990s alongside the expansion of fast‑food chains.
Non‑chocolate shakes often use real fruit purées, increasing their vitamin content.
There are "shake bars" where customers can mix several flavors into one drink.
Traditionally the shake is served in a tall glass with a straw, sometimes topped with whipped cream and sprinkles.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Milk, the main ingredient, is rich in calcium, which supports bone and teeth health.

items.title: Protein rich
items.content: Cream and milk provide complete protein that aids muscle repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk shakes contain vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotics (when yogurt is added)
items.content: If yogurt is used, the shake can help maintain a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Antioxidants (with fruit flavors)
items.content: Fruit additions like strawberry or blueberry supply vitamin C and polyphenols.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance should use lactose‑free milk or plant‑based alternatives.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweet syrups and flavorings can raise calorie count and blood glucose levels.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: Some flavors (e.g., nut) contain nuts and may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Excess calories
items.content: Large portions can contribute to weight gain if consumed frequently.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The shake is served cold, typically in a 300–500 ml glass. It is drunk through a straw and can also be used as a topping for pancakes, waffles or ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared shake should be kept in the refrigerator for no more than 2 hours. If components (milk, cream, fruit purée) are pre‑made, store them in sealed containers for up to 24 hours.
